newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 27.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 27.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** A 12 percent rise in freight rates announced in India's annual railway budget on Wednesday is likely to increase production costs and fuel inflation, leading industry organisations said.

Presenting the railway budget for 1997/98 in parliament, Railways Minister Ram Vilas Paswan said he planned to raise freight rates for all commodities, barring essentials, by 12 percent. The increases would apply to all distances and would be effective from April 1, 1997.

** The government on Wednesday said that its giant state-run railway network was in dire straits and its decades-old track system needed funds that were in short supply, but stopped short of talk about privatisation.

"I have no hesitation in informing this august house that the Indian Railways are passing through a very difficult phase," railway minister Paswan told parliament while unveiling the railway budget for 1997/98 (April-March).
** A 12 percent freight hike announced by the railways would raise costs and squeeze the margins of most sections of Indian industry, producers and analysts said.
It would hurt manufacturers of commodity products such as steel, cement and plastics most, they said on Wednesday.

** India's twitchy stock markets, frozen in the headlights of the federal budget, want to see strong government action rather than short-term policy palliatives, brokers and analysts said on Wednesday.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram will present the centre-left coalition government's 1997/98 (April-March) budget on Friday.
** India's National Stock Exchange (NSE) has set its sights on the Middle East after having revolutionised the country's stockmarket trading, bourse chief R.H. Patil said on Wednesday.
India's strict exchange control regulations are the only hurdle in the NSE's path, Patil told a news conference.
Plans to go overseas would depend on when the federal government decides to permit convertibility of the rupee on the capital account, Patil said.
MARKETS:
** Indian stocks at major bourses drifted on Wednesday, with the announcement of the railway budget having little impact on prices, dealers said.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's 30-share index rose 8.14 points, or 0.24 percent, to close at 3,364.97.
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index gained 2.75 points, or 0.28 percent, to 968.85
** The Delhi share index edged up 1.24 points to 728.26.
** The Calcutta share index climbed 1.76 points to 442.71.
** The Madras share index fell 9.47 points to 3,343.20.
